## Example input

**[your administration]:** PHEQA, Progressa's quality authority.

**[paste it]:** Clause 9 of PHEQA's contract with the supplier, as it stands:

> 9.1 The Supplier shall make changes to the Application only on a written Change Request approved by the Registrar. 9.2 Each change is accepted by PHEQA under clause 7 (Acceptance). 9.3 The Supplier shall correct any Defect notified by PHEQA within ten working days.

**[paste or adapt the description]:** The application is generated by a program from the application model, which is drawn from documents PHEQA has accepted. A correction is made in the document that owns the fact, carried into the model, and the application is generated again. A read-back program compares each generated file on the platform with what the model would generate, and marks it in step, out of date, or edited by hand.

## Example output

**Clause 9A — Generated files**

1. **No hand edits.** The Supplier shall not edit by hand any *Generated File* on the *Platform*, on any installation, including test installations.
2. **Corrections.** Every correction, including a change under a Change Request, shall be made in the *Accepted Description*. The Application shall then be generated again from it.
3. **Evidence.** Before each acceptance under clause 7, the Supplier shall run the *Read-back* and hand PHEQA its list of every Generated File and its mark. A delivery without the list shall not be accepted.
4. **Hand edits found.** A Generated File marked as edited by hand is a Defect under clause 9.3. The Supplier shall correct it in the Accepted Description and generate again, and PHEQA shall withhold 5 per cent of the milestone payment until the Read-back shows every file in step.

**Terms not defined in the pasted contract:** Generated File; Platform; Accepted Description; Read-back.

## Reading the output

### 1. The clause hooks into what the contract already has

Parts 3 and 4 lean on clause 7 (acceptance) and clause 9.3 (defects), so a hand edit gets the ten working days the contract already sets. That is the right instinct: the new clause adds a rule and its evidence, not a new procedure.

### 2. The 5 per cent was never asked for

Nothing in the pasted section mentions payments or milestones, yet part 4 withholds 5 per cent of one. "Milestone payment" is not even in the list of undefined terms. Whether PHEQA may withhold a payment, and how much, is set by the procurement rules that govern the contract; the assistant does not know them. This is why the clause goes to PHEQA's legal officer as a draft.

### 3. "Out of date" is left hanging

The read-back has three marks, and the clause deals with only one. A file marked out of date is not a hand edit, but it is not in step either. Decide whether part 3 should require every file in step before acceptance.

## What next

Put the reviewed clause beside the other requirements on the supplier in [6.1](../module-6/6-1.md). The read-back is not the only check worth writing into the contract: the checks on the platform's known traps follow in [5.3](./5-3.md).
